lines: Morgan Kim
+1 (555) 010-8173 | morgan.kim@example.com | example.com/code/mkim
EDUCATION
Clearwater Institute of Technology | B.S. in Electrical Engineering | Metro City, USA | Sep 2017 - May 2021
EXPERIENCE
Voltline Robotics | Embedded Software Engineer | Metro City, USA | Mar 2023 - Jun 2025
- Improved update speed by 60% by compressing firmware images and resuming interrupted downloads.
- Wrote a hardware-in-the-loop test rig that ran 400 motor-control tests on every firmware build.
- Added a crash logger that saved the last 2 seconds of sensor data to flash, which found the root cause of 5 field failures.
- Sampled the motor's 5 kHz vibration signal at 8 kHz so the fault detector could capture it without aliasing.
- Fixed a race condition on the counter shared by the interrupt handler and the main loop by declaring the counter volatile.
- Rewrote the motor-controller firmware for a warehouse robot fleet of 300 units, cutting control-loop jitter from 120 to 15 microseconds and field motor faults by 60%.
Clearwater Sensors | Hardware Test Engineer | Metro City, USA | Apr 2022 - Feb 2023
- Automated end-of-line tests for a humidity sensor, cutting test time per unit from 90 to 25 seconds across 20,000 units a month.
- Traced a batch of early field failures to a solder-paste change; the findings updated the reflow profile and cut returns from 2.1% to 0.4%.
- Wrote the calibration procedure for the sensor line, cutting calibration drift complaints from 15 to 2 a quarter.
- Designed a test fixture that checked 8 boards at once, raising station throughput from 40 to 150 boards an hour.
PROJECTS
Low-Power Weather Station | Independent Project | C, STM32 | Jan 2025 - Present
- Engineered a next-generation, innovation-driven IoT solution that redefines sustainable environmental sensing.
- Cut average current from 4.2 mA to 0.9 mA by sleeping between readings and batching radio transmissions.
- Published the schematics and firmware openly, and a local school built two stations from them.
Formula Student Electric Car | Electronics Lead, Team of 12 | C | Sep 2019 - May 2021
- Worked on firmware and testing for the robot fleet's motor controllers.
- The CAN-bus firmware for the dashboard was written and tested against the motor controller before each race.
- Rewrote motor-control firmware for a fleet of about 300 robots, cutting control-loop jitter eightfold and motor faults by more than half.
SKILLS
Tools: C, C++, STM32, oscilloscopes, FPGA
Methods: firmware, hardware-in-the-loop testing, CAN, low-power design

items.says: The code-profile link should be a complete, working URL that leads directly to relevant work.
items.because: A generic or inaccessible link adds little.

items.says: Consider putting Experience before Education.
items.because: With several years of experience, your most relevant evidence should appear first.

items.says: Use consistent punctuation, date formatting, and capitalization throughout.
Consider adding relevant academic distinctions, a strong technical project, or coursework if they fill a gap.
Clarify what “improved update speed by 60%” measures and give the conditions or baseline if possible.
items.because: It could mean faster transfer or shorter total update time.

items.says: Add evidence of the test rig’s value, such as coverage, defects caught, or time saved.
items.because: The bullet currently shows test volume but not its value.

items.says: Clarify whether the crash logger identified the causes or supplied data for an investigation.
Sampling a 5 kHz signal at 8 kHz cannot capture it without aliasing.
items.because: The sampling rate is below the Nyquist rate.

items.says: Declaring the shared counter volatile does not fix the race condition.
items.because: Volatile does not make access atomic or prevent a race between the interrupt handler and main loop.

items.says: Give the period or definition behind the reduction in field motor faults, if applicable.
items.because: It would clarify the relationship between the rewrite and the reported result.

items.says: The motor-controller accomplishment is repeated in Projects.
items.because: The Formula Student bullet claims nearly the same 300-robot fleet work and results.

items.says: Clarify that 20,000 units a month is the production volume covered by the change.
Clarify the comparison period or batch scope for the return rates.
Ensure the return-rate change can reasonably be attributed to the reflow-profile update.
Specify a comparable time period for the before-and-after complaint figures.
Make clear that the complaints relate to calibration drift.
Confirm that the before-and-after boards-per-hour figures use the same measurement conditions.
Replace or remove the generic claims about innovation and redefining sensing.
items.because: They are marketing language that does not show what you built or contributed.

items.says: Include the operating or sampling conditions behind the average-current measurements, if available.
items.because: The conditions would make the comparison interpretable.

items.says: Link to the published schematics and firmware and make sure they are accessible.
items.because: A reader should be able to verify or reproduce the project.

items.says: The bullet describes work on a robot fleet under a student electric-car project.
items.because: The work should be relevant to the Formula Student vehicle and your team role.

items.says: Replace the passive phrasing with what you personally owned or implemented.
items.because: The current phrasing obscures your contribution.

items.says: Clarify what testing before races demonstrated, if you can support it.
items.because: The result of the testing is unclear.

items.says: The 300-robot motor-control claim appears to duplicate the Voltline accomplishment.
items.because: It conflicts with the Formula Student project’s dates and setting.

items.says: Separate or regroup the Tools entries by type.
items.because: The category mixes languages, a microcontroller platform, test equipment, and an FPGA.

items.says: Clarify the toolchain or level of experience represented by FPGA, if applicable.
items.because: The entry leaves that experience unexplained.

items.says: Use a more specific category or term than “firmware” as a method.
items.because: Firmware is too broad to function as a method.

items.says: Categorize CAN as a protocol rather than a method.
items.because: The categories should distinguish protocols from practices.
